sources.entry: HomeServerHQ - All-in-one home server infrastructure and installer. Have a fully configured email server, VPN, and public website(s) set up in less than an hour, even behind CGNAT. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Shell

summary.one_liner: HomeServerHQ is a Bash-based all-in-one installer that sets up a home server plus a cloud VPS "RelayServer" to host email, VPN access, and public websites from behind CGNAT, with a bundle of integrated open source services.
summary.what_it_does: The installation and management utility installs both a HomeServer (at home) and a RelayServer (a rented VPS) along with a suite of bundled open source tools. The HomeServer creates an outgoing persistent WireGuard tunnel to the RelayServer, which handles incoming mail and https traffic so that email servers and public websites can run from home without opening ports on the router. The RelayServer includes a reverse proxy for websites, a Postfix mail relay with RSpamD spam detection and store-and-forward for up to 30 days, and port forwarding rules. The README says installed services are automatically added to Portainer, Caddy (https), Authelia (SSO), UptimeKuma (monitoring), and Heimdall (home page), and that databases are exported hourly with Ofelia. It also describes multi-domain hosting and joining or hosting other HomeServers in private networks. The README claims 160+ supported services and names Mailu as the mail server project.
use_cases: host an email server from home behind CGNAT
host public websites from a home server
remotely access home network from phone or laptop via VPN
set up a self-hosted home server with minimal IT knowledge
relay mail and https traffic through a cheap VPS
share a private network with other home servers
how_to_run: Alternatively, install a custom ISO (Debian 12 or Ubuntu 24, desktop or server) and double-click 'Install HSHQ'
Set up the RelayServer VPS via the HSHQ Web Utility (06 My Network -> 14 Set Up Hosted VPN)
notable: Two-server design: a HomeServer at home plus a lightweight RelayServer VPS that accepts public traffic, so no ports need opening on the home router
Mail relay routes incoming mail to the correct internal host and stores it for up to 30 days if the home server is unreachable
Each supported service is auto-integrated with reverse proxy, SSO, monitoring, and dashboard
Ships as custom Linux ISOs (Debian 12, Ubuntu 24) with a guided install
Ability to host multiple domains and networks, with a separate reverse proxy instance per network
caveats: Requires a rented VPS (README estimates $5-$10/month) plus a domain name; estimated ~$400 hardware and ~$15/month ongoing costs
Supported distributions are limited to Debian 12.9, Ubuntu 22.04/24.04, and Mint 22
IPv4 only at present; IPv6 is on the roadmap
Professional support is a paid subscription ($40/year per README); the project is otherwise free
